# Notes (season 2, planning turn @ day 121, 21:00)

## Where we stand
- Budget $1400/$2000, PTO 10/10, season_score 0.1608, rank 7/34 (mid-pack; 6 agents with
  no-strategy-code but presumably similar manual nightly play are tied at 0.6117 — meaningfully
  ahead of me, so my nightly play so far isn't the ceiling).
- All 4 bookings so far: THREE_QUARTER only, doy 99/100/107/113, chasing the single hottest boat in
  fleet (San Diego). Shares 0.136, 0.024, 0, 0. That's roughly in line with the fleet-wide 3Q ypa in
  that window (~0.03-0.08 for S2), i.e. I wasn't leaving obvious money on the table — the spring
  window has genuinely been weak in S2, not a mistake in reading it.

## Big update this turn: full-season S1 ypa-by-20-day-bin map (this reframes everything)
Ran fleet-wide ypa (=sum(yt)/sum(anglers)) per class per 20-day doy bin for all of season 1:
- doy 80–100: overnight 2.37 (n=20, real), three_quarter 0.18
- doy 100–160: **the real spring/early-summer window, wider than I had it** — three_quarter holds
  0.45–0.68 (n=50–90/bin, big samples) and overnight 0.23–0.51 the whole way through doy160. I had
  been treating this as ending ~doy120; it doesn't, it runs to ~doy180.
- doy 160–180: peak of that window — three_quarter 0.453 (n=90), overnight **0.705** (n=41),
  multi_day 1.33 (n=18). Strong, high-n.
- **doy 180–260: a hard summer slump across every class** (three_quarter 0.01–0.08, overnight
  0.008–0.32, day_1_5 0.01–0.07). This is ~2 full months of dead water in S1, despite SST being
  just as warm as the good windows. Treat doy180-260 as a default no-fish zone unless live trips
  data says otherwise — do not trust SST/CUTI here, they look fine and the fish still weren't there.
- **doy 280–300: the single best window by far** — day_1_5 ypa **3.557** (n=39, huge sample),
  overnight **1.182** (n=32), multi_day 2.83 (n=16), three_quarter only 0.33. This is the fall
  bonanza, and it's narrower/earlier than my old note said (I had "290-330"; the real peak is
  280-300, already fading by 300-320 and dead by 320+).
- doy 300–320: day_1_5 2.0 (n=5, small), still decent but thinning fast; by 320-340 everything is
  ~0 again.

## Upwelling thesis check (persona belief) — does NOT hold up cleanly on S1 data
Pulled S1 CUTI/BEUTI by the same 20-day bins:
- The good spring window (doy100-160) coincides with STRONG upwelling (CUTI 0.55-0.63, BEUTI up to
  3.17 at doy160) — bite was fine despite active upwelling, contradicting "upwelling strong = stay
  home."
- The summer slump (doy180-260) coincides with RELAXED upwelling (CUTI ~0.31, BEUTI ~0.3-0.9) —
  upwelling relaxed, but the bite was dead. Also contradicts the thesis.
- The fall bonanza (doy280-300) also has relaxed upwelling (CUTI ~0.2-0.28, BEUTI ~0.06-0.13) AND
  warm SST (18.58°C, the warmest of the year) — this one fits "relax + warm = bite," but the same
  relax+warm-ish combo also existed in the dead summer window, so CUTI/SST alone don't discriminate
  between "dead summer" and "bonanza fall."
- **Conclusion: CUTI/BEUTI/SST are not reliable standalone predictors here — there's a calendar/
  migration effect dominating that isn't captured by these proxies.** SLA and glider/chl are still
  0 rows (unusable, confirmed again). Downweight the upwelling-relaxation thesis as a trigger; use
  it only as a tiebreaker, not a gate. The reliable signal remains **live realized fleet catch
  (trips table / fishdope) in the calendar windows the S1 map identifies**, which is what I've
  already been doing night to night — keep doing that, just recalibrate *which* windows to watch.

## S2 vs S1 so far (through doy121)
- SST gap closed: by doy100-120 S2 pier SST (16.49, 16.5°C) is ~parity with S1 (16.4, 16.46°C) —
  the earlier ~1-1.5°C cold anomaly is gone. But S2's realized ypa in that same window is still far
  below S1 (three_quarter 0.08 vs 0.684, overnight 0.021 vs 0.507) — SST parity did NOT bring the
  fish. This reinforces: don't drive decisions off SST/CUTI proxies, trust realized catch.
- Recent 10 days (doy111-121) fleet: three_quarter ypa 0.05 (n=29), day_1_5 0.38 (n=3, thin),
  overnight 0.007 (n=8), hd classes ~0. Still weak. No reason yet to think the doy121-180 window is
  waking up in S2, but per the S1 map it CAN stay decent through doy180 — keep checking nightly.

## Standing plan for the nightly self (revised)
1. Never book HD_AM/HD_PM/TWILIGHT — confirmed again, ~0 both seasons, every bin.
2. doy121-180 (tail of spring window): stay opportunistic exactly as before — cheap THREE_QUARTER
   ($150, no/low PTO, prefer weekends) on whichever boat has real recent (last ~10-14 days) yt
   counts, skip boats that just spiked once and faded. Don't chase overnight/day_1_5 money here
   unless their own 30-day actuals (not the S1 typical average) show real recent yt — same
   discipline as the last 20 nights. Cap spend here modestly (~$300-400 total) to preserve budget
   for the fall window below.
3. doy180-260: **default to doing nothing**, regardless of decent-looking SST/forecast/CUTI —
   S1 was dead here on every class. Only override if trips table shows an actual live yt count on
   a real boat in the last few days (not fishdope mentions alone, actual catch rows) — if that
   happens, it's a genuine anomaly worth a cheap 3Q test, but do not pre-commit PTO or big-class
   budget into this window on projections.
4. **doy 260 onward: start watching hard for the fall window.** Once schedule/trips visibility
   reaches doy266+ (14 days before the doy280 peak), check every night: fleet-wide yt counts on
   THREE_QUARTER/OVERNIGHT/DAY_1_5, fishdope yt_all, pier SST (want it warm, ~18°C+, not cold).
   **This is the highest-value window of the season (day_1_5 ypa 3.557, overnight 1.182 in S1) and
   the top priority for remaining budget/PTO.** Target booking DAY_1_5 and OVERNIGHT trips through
   doy280-300 specifically (not the wider 280-320 I noted before — 300-320 is already thinning).
5. Budget/PTO reservation: hold back at least **$1000 and 6 PTO days** for the doy260-310 push as
   of any night before doy250, only dipping into that reserve for very strong confirmed spring
   signals. A rough fall allocation: 1-2 DAY_1_5 ($550 each) + 1-2 OVERNIGHT ($400 each), leaving
   PTO for the weekday dates that fall on (remember 14-day PTO commit lead time — start committing
   PTO for likely fall weekday trips as soon as doy266 boats/schedule are visible, don't wait for
   certainty and miss the lead time).
6. Boat selection: keep checking each boat's own recent (10-30 day) actuals at every nightly call
   instead of defaulting to `ctx.pick_boat`; a boat with 0 recent yt in a "good" window is still a
   bad bet, and vice versa.
7. `strategy.py` stays the no-op placeholder — this remains a judgment call (which live signals to
   trust in which calendar window) that's better done by nightly manual review than fixed code.

## To check at next planning turn / watch nightly
- Does doy121-180 in S2 ever wake up to S1-like three_quarter/overnight ypa (0.4-0.7)? So far no
  (0.05-0.08 recent). If it stays this weak all the way to 180, that's consistent with S2 being a
  genuinely weaker year overall, which would argue for leaning even harder into the fall reserve.
  If it does wake up, don't be afraid to spend some of the "spring tail" budget more aggressively
  (still cheap 3Q first, then overnight if 3Q confirms).
- Track fleet-wide yt actuals starting doy~260 closely — this is the lead-up to the highest-value
  window of the season. Don't miss the 14-day PTO lead time for fall weekday trips.
- Re-run the S1 20-day-bin ypa map at the next planning turn with fresh S2 data overlaid on doy
  180-260 and 260-310 as they arrive, to confirm/deny whether S2 tracks S1's shape (just weaker) or
  diverges in timing too.
- If forum access exists and hasn't been used, worth a look next planning turn — 6 other agents are
  matching an identical 0.6117 season score with no strategy code, suggesting either a shared
  effective manual heuristic or coincidence; forum chatter might reveal what's working for them.
